## Summary

Let $\bb{V}$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over a subfield of $\bb{R}$, and let $W$ be a finite group of automorphisms of $\bb{V}$ generated by reflections. Coxeter showed that $W$ admits a remarkable presentation in terms of generators and relations [@coxeter_1934]. Via this presentation, the group ring of $W$ can be deformed to a $\bb{Z}[\bm{q}^{\pm\frac{1}{2}}]$-algebra known as the Iwahori--Hecke algebra $H_W$. ## 

Let $S \subseteq W$ be the set of simple reflections in the chosen Coxeter presentation of $W$. Let $\mathit{Br}_W$ be the Artin braid group of $W$, and let $\mathit{Br}_W^+ \subseteq \mathit{Br}_W$ be the monoid of positive braids determined by $S$. Each element $s \in S$ lifts to an element $\sigma_s \in \mathit{Br}_W^+$, such that $\{\sigma_s\}_{s \in S}$ is a generating set for $\mathit{Br}_W^+$. ## 

A link in a $3$-manifold is the image of a disjoint union of finitely many circles under a smooth embedding. The HOMFLY series of a link in $S^3$ is a bivariate Laurent series that only depends on its isotopy class [@homfly].

Dunfield--Gukov--Rasmussen predicted [@dgr], and Khovanov--Rozansky constructed [@kr], a categorification of the HOMFLY series, sending a link in $3$-space to a triply-graded vector space over $\bb{Q}$. Appendix A. Coxeter Groups and Their Characters
A.1.
Our main reference for this appendix is the book [GP].
A Coxeter group is a group W that admits a ﬁnite presentation of the form
W = ⟨s ∈S : (st)ms,t = 1⟩,
where ms,s = 1 and ms,t ≥1 for all s, t ∈S. We say that W is irreducible iﬀit
is both nontrivial and not a product of smaller Coxeter groups. The pair (W, S) is
called a Coxeter system, and S is called its set of simple reﬂections. We say
that |S| is the rank of W.
If w ∈W, then an expression for w is a sequence (s1, . . . , sℓ) of elements of
